source_text: Ἡμεῖς γὰρ, ἀδελφοί, καὶ Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους ἀποστόλους ἀποδεχόμεθα ὡς Χριστόν· τὰ δὲ ὀνόματι αὐτῶν ψευδεπίγραφα ὡς ἔμπειροι παραιτούμεθα, γινώσκοντες ὅτι τὰ τοιαῦτα οὐ παρελάβομεν. ἐγὼ γὰρ γενόμενος παρ᾽ ὑμῖν ὑπενόουν τοὺς πάντας ὀρθῇ πίστει προσφέρεσθαι, καὶ μὴ διελθὼν τὸ ὑπ᾽ αὐτῶν προφερόμενον ὀνόματι Πέτρου εὐαγγέλιον εἶπον ὅτι εἰ τοῦτό ἐστι μόνον τὸ δοκοῦν ὑμῖν παρέχειν μικροψυχίαν, ἀναγινωσκέσθω· νῦν δὲ μαθὼν ὅτι αἱρέσει τινὶ ὁ νοῦς αὐτῶν ἐνεφώλευεν ἐκ τῶν λεχθέντων μοι, σπουδάσω πάλιν γενέσθαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς· ὥστε, ἀδελφοί, προσδοκᾶτέ με ἐν τάχει. ἡμεῖς δὲ, ἀδελφοί, καταλαβόμενοι ὁποίας ἦν αἱρέσεως ὁ Μαρκιανός, ὃς καὶ ἑαυτῷ ἠναντιοῦτο μὴ νοῶν ἃ ἐλάλει, ἃ μαθήσεσθε ἐξ ὧν ὑμῖν ἐγράφη. ἐδυνήθημεν γὰρ παρ᾽ ἄλλων τῶν ἀσκησάντων αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, τουτέστι παρὰ τῶν διαδόχων τῶν καταρξαμένων αὐτοῦ, οὓς Δοκητὰς καλοῦμεν (τὰ γὰρ φρονήματα τὰ πλείονα ἐκείνων ἐστὶ τῆς διδασκαλίας), χρησάμενοι παρ᾽ αὐτῶν διελθεῖν καὶ εὑρεῖν τὰ μὲν πλείονα τοῦ ὀρθοῦ λόγου τοῦ Σωτῆρος, τινὰ δὲ προσδιεσταλμένα, ἃ καὶ ὑπετάξαμεν ὑμῖν.
thought_title: Receiving apostles, rejecting forgeries, and the mixed gospel of Peter
orientation: Serapion, bishop of Antioch, opens his letter to the church at Rhossus by stating the principle that he and the church receive the apostles as Christ but reject writings falsely attributed to them, then recounts his earlier permission and his later discovery of heresy and of additions in the gospel attributed to Peter.
pass_a_gloss: For we, brothers, receive both Peter and the other apostles as Christ; but the forgeries in their name, as experienced men, we reject, knowing that we did not receive such things. For I, when I was with you, was supposing that you all were conducting yourselves in right faith, and not having gone through the gospel being brought forward by them in the name of Peter, I said that if this alone is what seems to you to be causing smallness of soul, let it be read; but now, having learned that their mind was lurking in some heresy from the things said to me, I will be eager to come to you again; so, brothers, expect me quickly. But we, brothers, having grasped of what heresy Marcion was, who also was contradicting himself, not understanding what he was saying, which things you will learn from what was written to you. For we were able, from others who had practiced this very gospel, that is, from the successors of those who had originated it, whom we call Docetists (for the thoughts, the greater part, are of that teaching), having used it from them, to go through it and to find that the greater part is of the true teaching of the Savior, but some things have been added, which things we also have appended for you.

choices.why: Glossary term; renders writings falsely attributed to an apostle without the banned 'false writings' or 'pseudonymous works'.
Glossary term; renders correct or sound Christian belief while avoiding the banned 'orthodox faith' and 'sound faith'.
Literal rendering of the compound to preserve the psychological sense of discouragement or pettiness of spirit.
Preserves the vivid animal-den metaphor of the verb (to lie in a den), matching the literal lane.
Glossary term; renders passages added to the gospel beyond the true teaching, avoiding 'inserted passages' and 'interpolations'.
Proper name of the heretic whose self-contradictory teaching Serapion mentions specifically as the type of heresy the community's mind was harboring.

pass_b_english: For we, brothers and sisters, receive Peter and the other apostles as we receive Christ, but as people with experience we reject the forgeries written in their name, knowing that we did not receive such things. When I was with you, I was supposing that all of you were conducting yourselves in right faith, and without examining the gospel they were putting forward under Peter's name, I said, "If this is the only thing that seems to cause you scruple, let it be read." But now, having learned from what was told to me that the mind of the community was harboring some heresy, I will make haste to come to you again. So, brothers and sisters, expect me soon.

But we, brothers and sisters, having grasped what kind of heresy Marcion belonged to—who was even contradicting himself, not understanding what he was saying, as you will learn from what has been written to you—we were able, from others who had studied this very gospel, that is, from the successors of those who originated it, whom we call Docetists (for most of their thoughts come from that teaching), to borrow it from them and go through it, and to find that most of it agrees with the true teaching of the Savior, but some things have been added, which we have also listed for you.
